chunk_findings.detail: The helper’s docstring says it runs the CLI with an OPEN stdin pipe when `stdin` is `None`, but `Popen.communicate(timeout=hang_s)` with `input=None` closes the child’s stdin because `communicate()` closes `self.stdin` whenever it exists, even with no input. Thus a command that would block reading stdin instead gets EOF and exits, so `_run` cannot detect the hang this regression is meant to catch. The code’s own comment (“communicate() closes stdin: use wait”) confirms the intended behavior, but the code does the opposite. The actual hang test works only by duplicating a raw `Popen` rather than using `_run`; a test using `_run(repo, "session", "prompt", "not-a-session")` on unfixed code would see EOF, return nonzero, and pass falsely.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_prompt_positional.py:_run

chunk_findings.detail: The timeout detection uses `-9` as the sentinel for a killed process, but that only holds for POSIX `SIGKILL`. On Windows, `Popen.kill()` calls `TerminateProcess` and the return code is typically `1`, not `-9`, so after the 90-second timer kills a hung command the assertion `p.returncode not in (0, -9)` still passes. In that environment the regression test would return successfully even when the bug is present.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_prompt_positional.py:test_words_in_the_session_slot_are_refused_not_read_from_stdin

chunk_findings.detail: The guard uses `if a.session and not A.session_known(...)`, so an explicit empty positional is mistakenly treated as “no session”. Given `ddflow session prompt ""` in an agent environment where stdin is a non-TTY open pipe with no data, `a.session` is `""`, the guard is skipped, `sys.stdin.isatty()` is false, and `sys.stdin.read()` blocks indefinitely. That is the same hang the fix is meant to refuse: the empty positional is not a session ID. It should check `a.session is not None` rather than truthiness.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/knowledge.py:_session_text

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims that a recognized session id still takes piped text, but the only assertion is `code == 0`. The supplied input `"piped words"` is never checked, so a bug where `_session_text` recognizes the id but silently ignores stdin (for example, records an empty string instead of the piped text) still returns 0 and the test passes. The regression coverage is vacuous for the behavior named.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_prompt_positional.py:test_a_known_session_id_still_takes_piped_text

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `sid in out or "latest" in out or "recorded" in out` does not verify that the text was recorded to the latest open session. A wrong implementation that always prints a generic line containing `"recorded"` or `"latest"` while actually recording to a newly created or different session would satisfy the test, so it does not catch the very latest-open-session routing it exists to protect.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding about explicit empty positional still holds in the shown diff. The added `_stdin_speaks` guard answers only the silent-pipe hang, but the gate remains `if a.session and not A.session_known(...)`. So `printf 'operator words' | ddflow session prompt ""` still treats the empty positional as “no session” (because `""` is falsey), skips the invalid-session-id refusal, sees the piped data/EOF as ready, reads `"operator words"`, and records it to the latest open session instead of refusing the non-session-id positional with a `--text` pointer. The silent-stdin probe does not answer this path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/knowledge.py:_session_text

chunk_findings.detail: The 3-second `select` timeout refuses valid piped text that is merely delayed. Given `sh -c 'sleep 4; echo words' | ddflow session prompt`, the pipe is open and initially silent; `select.select` returns no ready fd after 3 seconds, `_stdin_speaks` returns `False`, and the command exits with the “refusing to wait” error even though the piped input is neither an agent’s never-written pipe nor empty stdin. This is a new false negative introduced by the timeout.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/knowledge.py:_stdin_speaks

chunk_findings.detail: `select` reports EOF as readable, so `_stdin_speaks` returns `True` for an already-EOF empty stdin. Given `ddflow session prompt </dev/null`, the new guard is skipped, `sys.stdin.read()` returns `""`, and `_session_text` returns `""` rather than returning `None`/refusing. Thus the stated empty-stdin case is not refused by the gate added here; the empty string can be passed on as session text.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/knowledge.py:_stdin_speaks

The triage probe piping text does not refute this: the piped text supplies data and EOF, so `read()` returns; the hang remains when the pipe is open but has no data. The guard should test `a.session is not None`.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding about explicit empty positional still holds in the shown diff. chunk_findings.detail: The 3-second `select` timeout refuses valid piped text that is merely delayed. Given `sh -c 'sleep 4; echo words' | ddflow session prompt`, the pipe is open and initially silent; `select.select` returns no ready fd after 3 seconds, `_stdin_speaks` returns `False`, and the command exits with the “refusing to wait” error even though the piped input is neither an agent’s never-written pipe nor empty stdin. This is a new false negative introduced by the timeout.

chunk_findings.detail: `select` reports EOF as readable, so `_stdin_speaks` returns `True` for an already-EOF empty stdin. Thus the stated empty-stdin case is not refused by the gate added here; the empty string can be passed on as session text.

chunk_findings.detail: The test still does not exercise “latest open session” routing: it starts only one session and then asserts `_prompts(repo) == [(sid, "hello there")]`. With one session, `sid` is both the oldest and latest open session, so a wrong `_session_text` implementation that picks the first/oldest open session when several are open would record to that same sole `sid` and the test would pass. The added `(sid, text)` assertion fixes the old vacuous output check, but it still cannot distinguish the latest session from any other open session; to satisfy the name and intent, the test must start two sessions and assert the prompt is recorded on the second one.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `item: str = ""` parameter is inserted before the existing `agent: str = ""` parameter. This shifts `agent` for any positional caller of this public API. For example, `dupes("repo", "", False, None, 0, "agent-name")` previously used `"agent-name"` as the agent; after this change it binds `item="agent-name"` and leaves `agent=""`, so `_load` uses the default agent and the new unknown-item guard can reject an otherwise valid explicit agent. Append `item` after `agent` (or make it keyword-only) to preserve the existing positional contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/pairs.py:195 (dupes signature)

chunk_findings.detail: `pairs_from` applies the new `item` filter only after `pair_records(..., stop_after=stop_after)` has already stopped. If a caller passes a nonzero `stop_after`, `pair_records` can stop after producing earlier pairs, so a pair containing `item` later in the sweep is never present in `rows` and the post-filter returns `[]`. Example: records A, B, C; `stop_after=1` with `item="C"` returns only the A-B pair, and the item query wrongly reports no pair for C even though C has a duplicate beyond the first generated pair. The item restriction must be pushed into `pair_records`, or `stop_after` must be disabled when `item` is set.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/pairs.py pairs_from (post-filter after stop_after)

chunk_findings.detail: When `item` is non-empty, `pairs_from` now calls `pair_records(..., stop_after=0 if item else stop_after)`, which disables the caller's requested bound entirely instead of enforcing it after the item filter. If an item has multiple duplicate pairs (for example records A-B and A-C both contain A), `pairs_from(st, cfg, item="A", stop_after=1)` returns both rows, violating `stop_after=1`. The added test does not cover this because B4 has exactly one pair. The limit should be applied to the filtered rows after the `item` filter, not discarded.
